requirements.evidence: Main paths are in place: routes `entity.queues`/`entity.serve` (routes/web.php:59-60), every contract property and method on Queues (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:25-205) and Serve (Serve.php:28-89), members tabs with `role="tablist"` and whitelisted `setActiveTab` (Members.php:34-43, members.blade.php:5-14), navbar links (default-page.blade.php:49-56), and lang keys in both locales. Several details are wrong or missing. Rename passes the raw name as the slug (`slug: $this->renameName`, Queues.php:130) instead of re-deriving it, so renaming to "New" does not give slug `new`. The deactivate button and the confirm button always read `ui.queues_deactivate` (queues.blade.php:84,108), with no reactivate label for inactive queues. The access modal shows managers with the `ui.role_admin` tag (queues.blade.php:141) rather than as calling without a grant. The mode selector shows the raw values `any`/`priority_only`/`normal_only` and is labelled with `ui.serve_call_next` (serve.blade.php:19-24).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes correctly go through `CreateQueue`/`UpdateQueue`/`SetQueueAccess`/`CallNextTicket`, and the markup matches the members page's Bulma style. Deviations: `name` has `#[Validate]` but `create()` never calls `$this->validate()` (Queues.php:61-79); `renameName` and `mode` have no validation rules at all; `callableQueues()` is public, though conventions require internal helpers to be protected (Serve.php:50); there is no PHPDoc on the new public methods; there are no CHANGELOG or docs updates; and the waiting-list ordering and filter rules are re-implemented in the component (Serve.php:104-119) instead of coming from the domain.

security.evidence: Client ids are always resolved scoped to the entity (`$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail(...)`, `$this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail(...)`, Queues.php:83,107,164,175,189-190,199-200; Serve.php:65). Writes call `$this->authorize` and the domain actions. `accessQueue`/`accessGrants` are null or empty for foreign ids (Queues.php:213-219). `$entity` and `lastCalledTicketId` are `#[Locked]`, and output is escaped with `{{ }}`. Gaps: `mode` is client-writable and unvalidated, so `CallMode::from($this->mode)` (Serve.php:74) throws a ValueError (500) on tampered input; `renameName` is not validated; `callableQueues()` is a public endpoint; and the read-only modal actions (`openQueue`, `openAccess`, `startRename`) do not re-authorize. No exploitable unauthorized write was found.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: no tests/Feature for Queues, Serve, the member tabs, routes or the navbar, and no unauthorized-call or tamper tests. The conventions make these mandatory ("No production code without a test").

simplicity.evidence: Direct components with no extra layers, and existing `<x-label>`/`<x-input>` components are reused (queues.blade.php:41-42). There is some duplication: the nested-state reset block is repeated (Queues.php:86-91 vs 96-101), the ValidationException-to-addError loop is copy-pasted (Queues.php:68-72, 132-136), `Gate::forUser(auth()->user())` is redundant (Serve.php:54), and the ticket ordering is re-implemented (Serve.php:104-119).

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods that match the Members sibling. Minor oddities: `__('ui.queues_active', ['default' => 'Active'])` passes a meaningless replacement (queues.blade.php:21); the list's empty state reuses `ui.members_empty` (queues.blade.php:26); the section aria-label uses `ui.queues_title` without `:entity` (queues.blade.php:12); and `abort_if($queue === null, 404)` after a ternary with `findOrFail` is convoluted (Queues.php:148-152).

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the task: two components with their views, routes, lang keys, navbar links, and the members-page tab split (the move of the members-list box is part of that split). No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Two new Livewire components, two routes, tab behaviour and navbar changes ship without any Pest tests, including the mandatory unauthorized-call and tamper tests.
`rename()` passes `slug: $this->renameName` (the raw name) instead of a slug re-derived from it, so renaming "Old" to "New" does not yield slug `new`, and spaces or case reach the slug.
Public `mode` has no validation, so a tampered value makes `CallMode::from($this->mode)` throw a ValueError (500) instead of a validation error.
`name` is annotated with `#[Validate]` but `create()` never calls `$this->validate()`, and `renameName` has no rules, contrary to the Livewire validation rule.
`callableQueues()` is a public method and therefore a callable endpoint; internal helpers must be protected/private.
The toggle buttons always say "Deactivate", even for an inactive queue; the task asks for a reactivate label when the queue is inactive.
Managers in the access modal are tagged "Admin" (owners included) rather than shown as able to call without a grant.
The mode options show untranslated raw values, and the mode select is labelled with `ui.serve_call_next`, which breaks the all-text-from-lang rule and is a misleading accessible label.
There is no CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry and no docs update for the new pages and routes, and the new public methods have no PHPDoc.
The waiting-list order and the priority/normal filter are re-implemented in the component and may drift from `CallNextTicket`'s rules.
The aria-label uses `ui.queues_title` without `:entity`, `__()` is given a meaningless `['default' => ...]` replacement, and the empty state reuses `ui.members_empty`.
The nested-state reset is duplicated between `openQueue` and `closeQueue`, and the ValidationException-to-addError loop is copy-pasted between `create` and `rename`.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management and Serve Livewire pages, routes, navbar links, lang keys and the members-page tabs, calls the domain actions and correctly scopes every client id to the entity. It ships with no tests at all, which the project treats as a hard requirement, and rename does not derive a slug from the new name. Public properties (`mode`, `renameName`, `name`) are not validated, and there are smaller UX and contract gaps (no reactivate label, untranslated mode options), so it needs substantial rework before approval.
